name: Question 15
problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3}.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to its $x$-coordinate. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=-1.$
worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, the distance between a point and the line $y=-1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y+1|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=kx,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}kx\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k({\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{3}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =k\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot [y]_{0}^{3} \\  & =k(2-0)(3-0) \\  & =6k.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=kx=\frac{M}{6}x.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=-1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{M}{6}x|y+1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{M}{6}x(y+1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{M}{6}({\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{3}(y+1)^{2}\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{M}{6}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}(y+1)^{3}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{M}{6}\cdot \frac{1}{2}(4-0)\cdot [\frac{1}{3}(64-1)] \\  & =\frac{M}{6}\cdot 2\cdot \frac{63}{3} \\  & =7M.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

A rectangular plate of mass M occupies the region D={(x,y):0≤x≤2,0≤y≤3}. The mass density at each point is proportional to its x-coordinate. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line y=−1.

a
65M3
b
7M
c
7M3
d
65M9
e
64M9
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region D about an axis of rotation l is given by

Il=∬Dλ(x,y)[r(x,y)]2dA,

where λ(x,y) is the mass density function of the lamina, and r(x,y) is the distance from the line l to the point (x,y) on D.

First, the distance between a point and the line y=−1 is given by

r(x,y)=|y+1|.

Next, the mass density can be written as λ(x,y)=kx, where k is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of k by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

M=∬Dλ(x,y)dA=∫02∫03kxdydx=k(∫02xdx)(∫03dy)=k⋅[12x2]02⋅[y]03=k(2−0)(3−0)=6k.

Hence, λ(x,y)=kx=M6x. Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line y=−1 is

Il=∬Dλ(x,y)[r(x,y)]2dA=∫02∫03M6x|y+1|2dydx=∫02∫03M6x(y+1)2dydx=M6(∫02xdx)(∫03(y+1)2dy)=M6⋅[12x2]02⋅[13(y+1)3]03=M6⋅12(4−0)⋅[13(64−1)]=M6⋅2⋅633=7M.
